items.prose: Five seeds of one set-up end at validation losses 0.31, 0.35, 0.29, 0.33 and 0.32.
items.question: What is their sd, dividing by $n - 1$? Give 4 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Squared deviations from the mean, over $n - 1$, then the root.

byKey.var: That is the variance; take its root.

explain.text: The deviations from 0.32 are $-0.01, 0.03, -0.03, 0.01, 0$, with squares summing to 0.002. Over 4 that is 0.0005, whose root is 0.0224.

items.prose: A training log reads: data "spirals-600 v1", split seed 0, seed 3, the configuration, losses every 6 steps and one test score.
items.question: What stops an exact rerun?

options.why: Wall time is useful to log but changes no number in a rerun.
One test score is exactly right.

feedback.correct: Without the code version a rerun cannot be sure it runs the same training code.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Check each input a rerun needs.

byKey.wall: Wall time does not change the numbers.

explain.text: The inputs are code, data, split, seeds and settings. The code version is the one missing.

items.prose: Six paired seeds give differences, B minus A, of $-0.02$, $-0.01$, $-0.03$, $0.00$, $-0.02$ and $-0.01$.
items.question: What is the paired $t$? Give 2 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Mean, sd over $n - 1$, then $\bar d/(s_d/\sqrt 6)$.

explain.text: The mean is -0.015 and the sd 0.0105, so the standard error is 0.0043 and $t = -3.50$.

items.prose: A remove-one ablation of three changes runs every row on 5 seeds.
items.question: How many training runs, the full set-up included?

byKey.nofull: The full set-up needs its own 5 runs.

explain.text: The full set-up and three removals make 4 rows; $4 \times 5 = 20$ runs.

items.prose: Of ten seeds, two end at a validation loss near 0.70 and eight near 0.12.
items.question: Which summary is honest?

options.text: 2 of 10 seeds fail near 0.70; the other 8 average about 0.12
Mean about 0.24 over the ten seeds, with the sd
options.why: The mean falls between the two groups, where no seed ended.

options.text: About 0.12: the two failures are outliers to drop
options.why: They came from the same code; a new seed fails about twice in ten.

feedback.correct: Give the failure rate and the typical result of the runs that learned.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Ask what a new seed would do.

byKey.mean: A mean of two groups describes neither.
byKey.drop: Failures are part of the result.

explain.text: Two groups need two numbers: how often it fails, and how well it does when it works.

items.prose: Ten paired seeds give a mean difference of 0.03 with sd 0.02. Take $t_{0.975,\,9} = 2.262$.
items.question: What is the lower end of the 95% interval? Give 4 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Mean minus the half-width.

byKey.z: Use 2.262, not 1.96, with 9 degrees of freedom.

explain.text: The half-width is $2.262 \times 0.02/\sqrt{10} = 0.0143$, so the interval is 0.0157 to 0.0443, clear of 0.

items.prose: A new net trained on one batch of 8 points for 300 steps ends with a loss of 0.002 on that batch.
items.question: What has this check shown?

options.text: The model, loss and optimiser can learn: a working net memorises 8 points
The net will generalise well to new data from the same source
options.why: Memorising 8 points says nothing about new data; that is what validation is for.

options.text: It overfits the batch, so the set-up is broken and needs fixing
options.why: Overfitting one batch is the goal of this check, not a fault.

feedback.correct: It passes Karpathy's second step: the net can fit.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Ask what overfitting one batch tests.

explain.text: If a net cannot drive 8 points to near zero there is a bug. This one can, so the next step is to regularise.

items.prose: Four runs of a net over the same seeds: plain, 0.44; with a cosine schedule, 0.36; with warm-up, 0.39; with both, 0.34.
items.question: By how much does warm-up shrink the schedule's gain? Give 2 decimal places.

feedback.correct: Alone the schedule gains 0.08; with warm-up it gains $0.39 - 0.34 = 0.05$, so 0.03 less.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Find the schedule's gain with and without warm-up.

byKey.sign: The gain shrinks, so the answer is positive: 0.08 minus 0.05.
byKey.both: That compares both changes with the plain net.

explain.text: The schedule takes the loss from 0.44 to 0.36 alone, 0.08, but only from 0.39 to 0.34 with warm-up, 0.05. The interaction is 0.03: the two changes overlap.
